metaData.originalTitle: From Hype to Strong Foundations: What the Rise， Fall and Resurgence of Agents Can Teach Us About Outlasting the Cycle
metaData.title: From Hype to Strong Foundations: What the Rise， Fall and Resurgence of Agents Can Teach Us About Outlasting the Cycle
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This talk argues that building resilient AI agents requires embracing a stronger notion of agents, modular cognitive architectures, process science foundations, and terraforming the environment, drawing on lessons from past AI cycles.
metaData.summary: Aditya Kumarakrishnan, a Technical Fellow at Walmart Global Tech, presents a talk on building AI agents that can outlast the hype cycle. He identifies a pattern of 'catastrophic forgetting' where each AI peak and valley leads to relearning old lessons. The core of the talk is four foundational ideas often overlooked in current agent discourse. First, he advocates for a 'stronger notion of agents,' liberating the concept from being solely tied to LLMs and viewing it as a general-purpose, human-oriented computing abstraction. Second, he argues for building modular and extensible agents using a cognitive architecture (like CoALA), which allows for easy evolution from one agent architecture (e.g., ReAct) to another (e.g., CodeAct) without a full rewrite. Third, he emphasizes leveraging the mature field of process science, including workflow engines for durability and scalability, and process mining for discovering and understanding existing business processes. Finally, he introduces the concept of 'terraforming the environment' for agents, arguing that the most capable agent is limited by a hostile, non-ergonomic digital environment. He calls for reshaping systems to be more navigable, observable, and actionable for agents, moving beyond just adding an MCP interface.

mainPoints.point: Agents should be viewed as a general-purpose computing abstraction, not just an LLM in a loop.
mainPoints.explanation: This shifts the mindset from implementation-oriented to problem-driven, making agent design more future-proof and adaptable to new AI paradigms.

mainPoints.point: Modular cognitive architectures are essential for evolving agents without costly rewrites.
mainPoints.explanation: By decomposing an agent into well-defined modules (e.g., memory, action space), innovations like moving from ReAct to CodeAct become a simple swap of a module rather than a complete system rebuild.

mainPoints.point: Process science provides mature, battle-tested foundations for building durable and scalable agents.
mainPoints.explanation: Workflow engines offer built-in durability, scalability, and asynchrony, while process mining helps discover and codify existing business processes for agents to enact.

mainPoints.point: The environment agents operate in must be 'terraformed' for them to be effective.
mainPoints.explanation: Focusing solely on agent architecture while neglecting legacy systems, poor APIs, and a lack of guardrails limits agent success. The environment needs to be made more navigable and observable.

keyQuotes: The story of AI... is one of peaks and valleys. With each peak comes renewed fervor in building agents. With each valley comes this catastrophic forgetting of all of the lessons learned in the previous peak.
We should be liberating the agent from the LLM. We should be thinking about agents as a general-purpose computing abstraction.
The most capable agent is only as effective as the environment that it operates in. If you don't set up your agent for success by programming its environment, then it's doomed to fail.

relatedArticles.title: Introducing workspace agents in ChatGPT
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI introduces workspace agents, a new class of shared, long-running AI agents within ChatGPT for business teams, designed to automate complex workflows, integrate with organizational tools, and operate under enterprise-grade controls.

relatedArticles.title: Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Anthropic launches Claude Fable 5, a generally available Mythos-class model with state-of-the-art capabilities, alongside Claude Mythos 5 for trusted cybersecurity partners, with new safeguards to mitigate misuse risks.

relatedArticles.title: Leadership in AI-Assisted Engineering
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This presentation provides a research-backed playbook for engineering leaders on how to effectively measure, manage, and maximize the ROI of AI-assisted engineering, emphasizing a focus on throughput, psychological safety, and a multi-metric approach over top-down mandates.

relatedArticles.title: Using AI as a Thinking Partner for Large-Scale Engineering Systems
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: A Google Senior Staff Engineer shares a structured methodology for using AI as a thinking partner to understand, experiment with, and redesign a complex, multi-language, multi-repository engineering system.

relatedArticles.title: Introducing GPT-5.5
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI introduces GPT-5.5, a new category of AI that acts as an autonomous agent capable of planning, reasoning, and executing complex multi-step tasks across different applications.

relatedArticles.title: Engineering at AI Speed: Lessons from the First Agentically Accelerated Software Project
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article presents a case study of building Claude Code using Claude Code, detailing three stories that illustrate how AI changes bottlenecks in the software development lifecycle, emphasizing experimentation, architectural choices, and the importance of shipping to discover real requirements.

relatedArticles.title: The Claude Code Handbook: A Professional Introduction to Building with AI-Assisted Development
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: A comprehensive professional guide to Claude Code, Anthropic's agentic AI developer tool, detailing its capabilities, model selection, and the transformative shift toward AI-assisted software engineering.

relatedArticles.title: MCP in the Java World: Bringing Architectural Strategy to LLM Integrations
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: MCP Java SDK transforms LLM integration from ad-hoc tool calling into a disciplined architectural pattern, introducing protocol-level contracts, anti-corruption layers, and governance for enterprise Java systems.

relatedArticles.title: What I Learned Building Multi-Agent Systems From Scratch
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: A staff engineer at Shopify shares the journey of building multi-agent systems from scratch, revealing that narrow-focused agents outperform generalists, and that empowering domain experts with tools is more effective than creating an AI SWAT team.

relatedArticles.title: Codex Now Integrates Directly with Chrome on macOS and Windows
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI introduces a new Chrome extension for Codex on macOS and Windows, enabling the AI to operate directly within a user's live browser session to perform complex, parallel automation tasks using their active profile and direct code execution.
